sections.theory:
The compounds in which chromium shows +6 oxidation state are chromium trioxide (CrO₃), potassium chromate (K₂CrO₄) and potassium dichromate (K₂Cr₂O₇) etc.

14.3.2.2 Chromate – Dichromate Equilibrium

When solid potassium chromate, K₂CrO₄, is dissolved in water it forms a yellow solution. When solid potassium dichromate, K₂Cr₂O₇, is dissolved in water the resulting solution is orange. The colours come from the negative ions CrO₄²⁻(aq) and Cr₂O₇²⁻(aq). However, in solution these ions are actually in equilibrium as indicated by the equation:

2CrO₄²⁻(aq) + 2H⁺(aq) ⇌ Cr₂O₇²⁻(aq) + H₂O(l)

This is dynamic equilibrium and sensitive to the acidity and basicity of solution. According to Le-Chatelier’s principle, the addition of acid to the reactant shifts the equilibrium towards right and yields more dichromate (orange). On the other hand, the addition of base promotes the conversion of dichromate to chromate.

2OH⁻ + Cr₂O₇²⁻ ⇌ 2CrO₄²⁻ + H₂O

Orange — Yellow

14.3.2.3 Reduction of Chromate (VI) Ions with Zn and an Acid

Dichromate (VI) ions (for example, in potassium dichromate (VI) solution) can be reduced to chromium (III) ions and chromium (II) ions using zinc and either dilute sulphuric acid or hydrochloric acid.

Acidic potassium dichromate solution reacts with zinc forming Cr³⁺ ions and colour of the solution changes from orange to green.

For reduction from +6 to +3,

Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 3Zn → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O + 3Zn²⁺

and then after further reduction by the zinc, Cr⁺² ions are formed and colour changes from green to blue.

For reduction from +3 to +2

2Cr³⁺ + Zn → 2Cr²⁺ + Zn²⁺

14.3.2.4 Potassium Dichromate as an Oxidizing Agent in Organic Chemistry

Potassium dichromate (VI) is used as an oxidizing agent in organic reactions. The solution of potassium dichromate (VI) is acidified with dilute sulphuric acid. When oxidation occurs, the orange solution containing the dichromate (VI) ions is reduced to a green solution containing chromium (III) ions.

i. Primary Alcohols

Primary alcohol are oxidized to either aldehydes or carboxylic acids depending on the reaction conditions.

In the case of the formation of carboxylic acids, the alcohol is first oxidized to an aldehyde, which is then oxidized further to the acid.

Partial Oxidation to Aldehydes

We get an aldehyde if we use an excess of alcohol and remove aldehyde as soon as it is formed in order to avoid further oxidation.

3CH₃CH₂OH + Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 8H⁺ → 3CH₃CHO + 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O

primary alcohol — Acetaldehyde

Full Oxidation to Carboxylic Acids

The alcohol is heated with an excess of the oxidizing agent i.e. potassium dichromate (VI), on completion of the reaction, the carboxylic acid is produced.

3CH₃CH₂OH + 2Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 16H⁺ → 3CH₃COOH + 4Cr³⁺ + 11H₂O

primary alcohol — ethanoic acid

ii. Secondary Alcohols

Secondary alcohols are oxidized to ketones. When the secondary alcohol, 2-propanol is heated with potassium dichromate (VI) solution acidified with dilute sulphuric acid, ketone (propanone) is produced.

Conc. H₂SO₄; 2-propanol (Secondary alcohol) → ketone

iii. Tertiary Alcohols

Tertiary alcohols are not oxidized by acidified sodium or potassium dichromate(VI) solution.

+6 سے +3 تک تخفیف کے لیے،

پھر زنک سے مزید تخفیف کے بعد Cr⁺² آئن بنتے ہیں اور رنگ سبز سے نیلا ہوتا ہے۔

+3 سے +2 تک تخفیف کے لیے

2Cr³⁺ + Zn → 2Cr²⁺ + Zn²⁺

14.3.2.4 نامیاتی کیمیا میں پوٹاشیم ڈائی کرومیٹ بطور تکسیدی عامل

پوٹاشیم ڈائی کرومیٹ(VI) نامیاتی تعاملات میں تکسیدی عامل ہے۔ اس کا محلول پتلے سلفیورک تیزاب سے تیزابی بنایا جاتا ہے۔ تکسید ہو تو ڈائی کرومیٹ(VI) آئنوں والا نارنجی محلول تخفیف پاکر کرومیم(III) آئنوں والا سبز محلول بنتا ہے۔

i. ابتدائی الکوحل

ابتدائی الکوحل تعامل کی شرائط کے لحاظ سے ایلڈیہائیڈز یا کاربوکسلک تیزابوں میں تکسید پاتے ہیں۔

کاربوکسلک تیزاب بننے کی صورت میں الکوحل پہلے ایلڈیہائیڈ میں تکسید پاتا ہے، جو پھر مزید تکسید سے تیزاب بنتا ہے۔

ایلڈیہائیڈز میں جزوی تکسید

الکوحل کی زائد مقدار استعمال کریں اور ایلڈیہائیڈ بنتے ہی نکال دیں تاکہ مزید تکسید نہ ہو تو ایلڈیہائیڈ حاصل ہوتا ہے۔

3CH₃CH₂OH + Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 8H⁺ → 3CH₃CHO + 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O

ابتدائی الکوحل — ایسیٹ ایلڈیہائیڈ

sections.content:
The compounds in which chromium shows +6 oxidation state are chromium trioxide (CrO₃), potassium chromate (K₂CrO₄) and potassium dichromate (K₂Cr₂O₇) etc.

14.3.2.2 Chromate – Dichromate Equilibrium

When solid potassium chromate, K₂CrO₄, is dissolved in water it forms a yellow solution. When solid potassium dichromate, K₂Cr₂O₇, is dissolved in water the resulting solution is orange. The colours come from the negative ions CrO₄²⁻(aq) and Cr₂O₇²⁻(aq). However, in solution these ions are actually in equilibrium as indicated by the equation:

2CrO₄²⁻(aq) + 2H⁺(aq) ⇌ Cr₂O₇²⁻(aq) + H₂O(l)

This is dynamic equilibrium and sensitive to the acidity and basicity of solution. According to Le-Chatelier’s principle, the addition of acid to the reactant shifts the equilibrium towards right and yields more dichromate (orange). On the other hand, the addition of base promotes the conversion of dichromate to chromate.

2OH⁻ + Cr₂O₇²⁻ ⇌ 2CrO₄²⁻ + H₂O

Orange — Yellow

14.3.2.3 Reduction of Chromate (VI) Ions with Zn and an Acid

Dichromate (VI) ions (for example, in potassium dichromate (VI) solution) can be reduced to chromium (III) ions and chromium (II) ions using zinc and either dilute sulphuric acid or hydrochloric acid.

Acidic potassium dichromate solution reacts with zinc forming Cr³⁺ ions and colour of the solution changes from orange to green.

For reduction from +6 to +3,

Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 3Zn → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O + 3Zn²⁺

and then after further reduction by the zinc, Cr⁺² ions are formed and colour changes from green to blue.

For reduction from +3 to +2

2Cr³⁺ + Zn → 2Cr²⁺ + Zn²⁺

14.3.2.4 Potassium Dichromate as an Oxidizing Agent in Organic Chemistry

Potassium dichromate (VI) is used as an oxidizing agent in organic reactions. The solution of potassium dichromate (VI) is acidified with dilute sulphuric acid. When oxidation occurs, the orange solution containing the dichromate (VI) ions is reduced to a green solution containing chromium (III) ions.

i. Primary Alcohols

Primary alcohol are oxidized to either aldehydes or carboxylic acids depending on the reaction conditions.

In the case of the formation of carboxylic acids, the alcohol is first oxidized to an aldehyde, which is then oxidized further to the acid.

Partial Oxidation to Aldehydes

We get an aldehyde if we use an excess of alcohol and remove aldehyde as soon as it is formed in order to avoid further oxidation.

3CH₃CH₂OH + Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 8H⁺ → 3CH₃CHO + 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O

primary alcohol — Acetaldehyde

Full Oxidation to Carboxylic Acids

The alcohol is heated with an excess of the oxidizing agent i.e. potassium dichromate (VI), on completion of the reaction, the carboxylic acid is produced.

3CH₃CH₂OH + 2Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 16H⁺ → 3CH₃COOH + 4Cr³⁺ + 11H₂O

primary alcohol — ethanoic acid

ii. Secondary Alcohols

Secondary alcohols are oxidized to ketones. When the secondary alcohol, 2-propanol is heated with potassium dichromate (VI) solution acidified with dilute sulphuric acid, ketone (propanone) is produced.

Conc. H₂SO₄; 2-propanol (Secondary alcohol) → ketone

iii. Tertiary Alcohols

Tertiary alcohols are not oxidized by acidified sodium or potassium dichromate(VI) solution.
